Subject: Embeddings migration & SDK integration — next steps

Hi Sara — great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so we have alignment: 

Summary of your current state:
- Using OpenAI ada-002 embeddings (1536 dims) for semantic search + reranker.
- Index in Pinecone, occasional latency spikes at peak query QPS.
- Historical backfill of ~1.8M documents; recent daily add rate ~8k docs/day.

Key risks you flagged:
- Migration risk: search relevance changing with new embeddings
- Cost of re-embedding historical data
- Auth/networking constraints for private datasets in your VPC

Redwood recommendations / immediate asks:
1) Vector dimensions: we recommend maintaining 1536 dims to preserve parity with ada-002 unless you want to trade quality for smaller footprint (512).
2) Normalization: L2-normalize vectors on write and use cosine similarity for retrieval — Redwood SDK can handle normalization during embedding calls.
3) Batching: for your backfill, use batch size 256-512 depending on compute; we'll suggest 256 as conservative for predictable latency.
4) Routing & auth: use the embeddings route "embeddings-prod-us-1". Auth via short-lived service principal tokens for large backfills (we can provide a signed-service-account flow; keys rotated via KMS).
5) Reranker strategy: keep current reranker in the loop for A/B tests. We can run simultaneous scoring with both embeddings sets to measure delta.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa (us): share migration plan + SDK setup snippets (attached).
- Acme: confirm preferred vector dim (1536 vs 512) and whether you want a canary re-embed for a subset of content.
- Schedule technical working session (30–45m) to walk SDK auth and incremental backfill options.

Attachments: acme-migration-plan.pdf (migration checklist + estimate), sdk-setup-snippets.txt (auth + sample code)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a tentative slot for the technical session.
\Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifying questions before the tech session: 

1) We currently use "ada-002" embeddings (1536). If we keep 1536 dims with Redwood, is there any expected distributional shift that would impact our reranker? Can we run both side-by-side?
2) For normalization: our current pipeline does no explicit L2 normalization (Pinecone handles cosine). If we normalize on write with Redwood SDK, will that change values stored in Pinecone or do we need a full reindex?
3) Backfill compute cost: can you share a rough cost estimate for re-embedding 1.8M docs at 1536 dims? We need to budget for compute + read/write to our index.
4) Network constraints: our data team prefers outbound-only connections; can Redwood's Private deployment (VPC peering) support the re-embed without opening inbound ports?

Happy to join a technical working session — Tue/Wed next week after 10am PST works for me.

Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Embeddings migration & SDK integration — next steps

Hi Sara — quick answers inline, plus additional technical notes we can walk through during the session.

1) Distributional shift / A/B: You can absolutely run both embeddings side-by-side. Our recommendation is a canary where 10% of queries are scored by Redwood embeddings while the rest remain on ada-002; compare top-k overlap and reranker metrics (MRR, NDCG). We also offer a rerank-only comparison where we feed the same candidates to your current reranker to quantify delta.

2) Normalization & index consequences: If you L2-normalize on write and send normalized vectors to Pinecone, you will need to reindex the stored vectors (i.e., write normalized versions). Pinecone's cosine search is equivalent to dot product on L2-normalized vectors. Redwood's SDK can output normalized vectors directly so you can do an incremental reindex (no need to mutate other metadata). For a phased approach: re-embed and index a small partition first (e.g., 5–10%) and compare.

3) Backfill cost estimate (very rough):
- 1.8M docs at 1536 dims
- With batching 256 and compute using a standard GPU worker pool: estimate ~12–18 hours wall-clock depending on concurrency.
- Cost ballpark (compute + network + storage writes): ~$4k–$9k one-time for the re-embed (we'll run a more detailed estimate with your exact dataset shape).

4) Network / Private deployment: yes — we can run the re-embed inside your VPC using Redwood Private (VPC peering or private link). That allows outbound-only connections from your side and avoids exposing public inbound endpoints. We'll coordinate with your infra team for the peering setup and service account auth.

SDK/Auth snippet (example):
- Use short-lived service principal tokens for large jobs. Sample pseudocode:

# PSEUDOCODE
client = RedwoodClient(auth="service-principal", scope="embeddings-prod-us-1")
for batch in chunk(docs, 256):
  vectors = client.embeddings.create(input=batch, normalize=true, model="redwood-emb-1536")
  indexClient.upsert(namespace="acme-docs", items=vectors)

Notes:
- Model: redwood-emb-1536 is our parity model for ada-002.
- normalize=true performs L2 normalization before returning vectors.
- We recommend HNSW indexing with ef_construction tuned for low-latency retrieval.

I'll attach SDK snippets and the migration checklist we mentioned earlier (attached).
\Would you and your infra lead be available Tue 2026-07-22 11:00am PST for the working session?
\Best,
Marissa

\- Migration compute: If you choose Redwood-managed backfill on Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), we can commit a 2–4 hour window per shard and parallelize across nodes. If you self-run via SDK against our hosted embeddings API, cost will be usage-based (per-embedding call).
- Ballpark pricing: for 1.8M docs at 1536 dims, estimate of $4k–$9k Marissa mentioned assumes hosted inference rates + IO. Dedicated reserved capacity options would give you greater cost predictability — we can run exact cost modeling for the deal.
- Timeline: technical working session Tue (per Marissa) then 1 week for a canary re-embed and 2–3 additional weeks for full backfill + index verification depending on infra windows.
